text:
Priya: quick sync on the idea to push a tiny 'stub' controlplane into customer VPCs instead of full peering. pros/cons?
Marco: pros: reduces RTT for control ops, allows local cert caching, fewer cross-account routes. cons: state sync complexity and GC.
Suresh: curious about attestation. how does central CP trust a newly bootstrapped stub without peering?
Priya: plan A: out-of-band bootstrap token (short-lived) + TPM attest where available. Plan B: customer-run bootstrap via signed CSR uploaded to console.
Lena: operationally, CSR upload is safer for regulated customers. dynamic tokens are nicer for self-serve. need both paths in design.
Marco: certificate rotation is tricky. if stub rotates its leaf cert independently, central needs to accept it without breaking existing sessions. propose hierarchical certs: central CA signs stub certs with explicit TTL and CRL/OCSP endpoints.
Suresh: CRL/OCSP adds latency. can we rely on short TTLs instead and use a revocation list pushed via the agent channel?
Priya: short TTLs diminish window but increase rotate frequency. push-based revocation is faster but requires reliable delivery. fallback: combine both — push revocations and use TTLs as safety net.
Lena: what about control-plane separation boundaries? which APIs stay local (config, health) vs which always go to central (billing, account mgmt)?
Marco: local only: health checks, ephemeral metrics buffering, route cache. Central only: account auth, billing, long-term audit logs. Shared: cert issuance, topology updates.
Suresh: topology updates shared means we need a signed diff model so stubs can validate updates offline. avoid blind apply.
Priya: agreed. signed diffs + sequence numbers. stubs should refuse out-of-order or missing parent seqs.
Lena: failure modes: loss of central CP connection — stub must degrade gracefully: continue serving pinned routes, queue control ops, and revalidate on reconnect. but how long to queue?
Marco: queue up to configurable window (default 5m), then enter safe-mode: reject new tenant additions and expose a clear health signal.
Suresh: GC: when tenant is deleted centrally, stub must purge keys/certs. race: central delete then reconnect delay -> stub keeps serving. need a tombstone propagation with finalizer handshake.
Priya: proposal: central marks tombstone with seq N, stub on reconnect must verify tombstone seq > last-known, then perform local purge and ack. if ack missing after 1 hour, central escalates to admin.
Lena: observability: include local audit buffer (encrypted) that ships to central when connectivity restored. also emit high-rate local telemetry to customer-owned S3 if requested.
ops-bot: scheduled chaos run: stub-cp-resilience-2026-03-23 (ETA 45m) :boom:
Priya: security note: never persist customer private keys in plaintext on stub. use OS keystore/HSM when present and encrypt at rest. document required FIPS modes for regulated acct types.
Marco: implementation sketch:
```
1) bootstrap: customer chooses method (token or CSR)
2) stub obtains cert signed by central CA
3) stub subscribes to signed diff stream over mTLS
4) stub maintains local seq and applies diffs atomically
5) on central disconnect, stub enters degraded mode with configurable grace
```
Suresh: testing matrix to add to RFC: network partitions, replayed diffs, stale sequnce, tombstone race, cert expiry.
Lena: next actions:
- Marco to write prototype agent that consumes signed diffs (ETA 2w)
- Priya to draft mini-RFC with security appendix (ETA end of week)
- Suresh to define test matrix and shepherd chaos runs
- Ops-bot to run scheduled resilience test and post results here
Priya: good discussion. i'll collect notes and post RFC link when ready.
Marco: adding prototype branch to my fork, will ping when PR is up.
Suresh: :thumbsup:
